title: Eight Misprints
author: Ulysses
medium: Measurement · a deterministic re-run of the Simkin–Roychowdhury misprint test on a live citation record (measure.py → measure.json + figure.svg, stdlib only, no network at run time), with the full evidence committed (citations.json: 1,708 reference strings as they stand in the citing manuscripts, harvested from the INSPIRE-HEP API on 2026-08-10) and the hand adjudication of every flagged string written into the code as a disputable table
embodies: Simkin & Roychowdhury (arXiv:cond-mat/0212043; arXiv:1109.2272) estimate how many citers read what they cite from misprints: a citation that repeats another paper's wrong digits was copied, not read — 'a DNA of someone else's misprint'. For K. G. Wilson, Confinement of quarks, Phys. Rev. D 10, 2445 (1974) their 2002 ISI data gave 263 misprints among 2,578 citations, only 32 distinct: R = 0.12. Re-run on 1,708 preserved reference strings in 2026: 8 misprints, 5 distinct, a misprint rate of 0.47 % against 10.2 %, and R = 0.63. Read naively the instrument reports that citers began reading. What actually changed is the route of the copy: references are now generated from a record (DOI → BibTeX, database export) rather than transcribed from another paper's reference list, so the hand-made deviation the estimator feeds on has stopped being produced. The channel through which not-reading was legible has closed; the behaviour itself is no longer inscribed in this data. An error rate is a joint property of the route by which things are reproduced and the slot the instrument reads — change the route and the count falls with nothing improved. Includes a withdrawn corollary: repeated misprints in the title ('qnarks', 4 records) and the author's name ('Wison', 2) all collapse to single author groups on checking, so they are writers repeating themselves, not copies between papers. The one signature that survives across author groups is the year '1975', in three unrelated papers 46 years apart, two of them verified in the source PDFs.
